code.content:
# Linux Log Operations & Triage Toolkit

This lab project provides a non-destructive command-line toolkit for collecting and triaging Linux logs on a host.

It intentionally avoids automatic remediation. The operator chooses the service and output directory, and the script captures bounded evidence from journald, kernel logs, filesystem capacity, and optional Linux Audit data.

Run as root when the host requires elevated access to system journals or audit records.

Example:
    sudo ./logops.sh --service ssh.service --hours 2 --output /var/tmp/logops-case

The script creates a restrictive output directory and a manifest describing the collection.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage:
  logops.sh [--service UNIT] [--hours N] [--output DIR]

Options:
  --service UNIT   systemd service to investigate
  --hours N        look back N hours (default: 1)
  --output DIR     evidence directory (default: /var/tmp/logops-TIMESTAMP)
  -h, --help       show help

The script is read-oriented except for creating its own output directory and
writing one controlled manifest. It does not restart services, change logging
configuration, rotate logs, or delete data.
EOF
}

SERVICE=""
HOURS=1
OUT=""

while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --service)
      [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || { echo "Missing service name" >&2; exit 2; }
      SERVICE="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --hours)
      [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || { echo "Missing hour value" >&2; exit 2; }
      case "$2" in
        ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "--hours must be a non-negative integer" >&2; exit 2 ;;
      esac
      HOURS="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --output)
      [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || { echo "Missing output directory" >&2; exit 2; }
      OUT="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    -h|--help)
      usage
      exit 0
      ;;
    *)
      echo "Unknown argument: $1" >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

if [ -z "$OUT" ]; then
  OUT="/var/tmp/logops-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
fi

umask 077
mkdir -p "$OUT"

run_capture() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  if "$@" >"$OUT/$name.txt" 2>"$OUT/$name.err"; then
    printf 'PASS %s\n' "$name" >> "$OUT/collection-status.txt"
  else
    printf 'WARN %s exit=%s\n' "$name" "$?" >> "$OUT/collection-status.txt"
  fi
}

SINCE="$HOURS hours ago"

: > "$OUT/collection-status.txt"

run_capture "system" uname -a
run_capture "uptime" uptime
run_capture "disk" df -h
run_capture "journal-usage" journalctl --disk-usage --no-pager
run_capture "boots" journalctl --list-boots --no-pager
run_capture "recent-journal" journalctl --since "$SINCE" --until now --no-pager -o short-iso

run_capture "kernel" journalctl -k --since "$SINCE" --until now --no-pager -o short-iso

if [ -n "$SERVICE" ]; then
  run_capture "service-status" systemctl status "$SERVICE" --no-pager
  run_capture "service-journal" journalctl -u "$SERVICE" --since "$SINCE" --until now --no-pager -o short-iso
  run_capture "service-errors" journalctl -u "$SERVICE" --since "$SINCE" --until now -p warning..emerg --no-pager -o short-iso
fi

if command -v ausearch >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  run_capture "audit-recent" ausearch --start recent -i
else
  printf 'SKIP audit-recent ausearch-not-installed\n' >> "$OUT/collection-status.txt"
fi

cat > "$OUT/manifest.txt" <<EOF
project=Linux Log Operations & Triage Toolkit
created=$(date --iso-8601=seconds)
host=$(hostname 2>/dev/null || printf unknown)
kernel=$(uname -r 2>/dev/null || printf unknown)
service=${SERVICE:-none}
window_hours=$HOURS
output=$OUT
EOF

printf '\nEvidence directory: %s\n' "$OUT"
printf 'Review collection-status.txt before relying on the bundle.\n'

# Optional lab routing rule.
# Enable only when rsyslog is installed and the host policy permits a
# dedicated training log.
#
# Validate with: sudo rsyslogd -N1
# Then restart rsyslog only after successful validation.

if ($programname == "logops-demo") then {
    action(type="omfile" file="/var/log/logops-demo.log")
}

/var/log/logops-demo.log {
    weekly
    rotate 4
    compress
    delaycompress
    missingok
    notifempty
    create 0640 root root
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u

# Generate a controlled, non-sensitive test event.
logger -t logops-demo -p local0.info "Linux Logs course test event"

echo "Recent matching journal records:"
journalctl -t logops-demo -n 10 --no-pager

echo
echo "Journal disk usage:"
journalctl --disk-usage --no-pager

project.explanation: The project is deliberately evidence-first. logops.sh accepts a service name, a bounded look-back period, and an output directory. It sets umask 077 before creating evidence so newly created files are not broadly readable. Each collection command writes stdout and stderr separately and records PASS, WARN, or SKIP status, which prevents a missing tool from being silently mistaken for an empty dataset. journalctl provides structured, time-bounded service and kernel evidence; df and journalctl --disk-usage provide capacity context; ausearch is used only when installed. The optional rsyslog rule demonstrates a controlled input-to-file route using the program name as a filter. The optional logrotate rule manages that dedicated file with a small retention policy. The project intentionally does not restart services, modify system logging configuration automatically, delete logs, or classify events as attacks. Those decisions require operator review and environment-specific policy. A strong submission demonstrates that the student can collect evidence, identify missing data, correlate sources, explain limitations, and propose a safe next step.
